stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple is barely off its 52‑week high, trading just 0.0% below that peak, while up 27.1% YTD and modestly positive on the day and week. The stock remains near the top of its range after a strong rally, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and any macro‑tech demand shifts.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft sits 2.6% below its 52‑week high, up 50.2% from the low and gaining 12.6% YTD, though it slipped 1.9% today. With the price anchored in the upper third of its range, the next catalyst is the company’s quarterly results and cloud spending trends.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA is 10.5% under its 52‑week high, still 29.9% above the low and up 13.7% YTD, but has underperformed the week with a 6.6% decline. Investors should focus on the upcoming GPU demand outlook and any guidance on AI‑related revenue.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet trades 15.3% below its 52‑week high, 36.3% above its low, and is up 8.3% YTD despite recent declines. The key watch is the next earnings report and ad‑spending trends that could dictate whether the stock can reclaim higher ground.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon is 12.0% off its 52‑week high, 25.8% above its low, and up 10.4% YTD, with a modest dip today. The pivotal factor will be the upcoming retail and cloud earnings, especially any signs of margin pressure.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta Platforms sits 8.8% below its 52‑week high, 35.2% above its low, and is up 9.3% YTD, though it fell 3.7% on the day. Investors should monitor the next earnings for ad revenue trends and progress on its metaverse investments.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla is 27.6% under its 52‑week high but still 18.9% above its low, and is down 19.0% YTD, with a recent slide across all time frames. The next catalyst is production and delivery guidance, plus any updates on pricing strategy and cost controls.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom is 31.5% below its 52‑week high, only 12.4% above its low, and is down 4.9% YTD after a sharp weekly drop. Investors should watch the upcoming earnings for signs of margin recovery and the impact of its recent acquisitions.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD trades 18.6% below its 52‑week high but remains 176.9% above its low, boasting a massive 136.6% YTD gain despite a 6% daily decline. The key focus is the next earnings beat and the sustainability of its chip demand amid competitive pressures.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 14.5% over the month and sits 55.4% below its 52‑week high, edging just above its low. The recent 4.6% daily drop underscores weakness in enterprise software demand. Investors should watch the upcoming earnings guidance and any cloud‑services margin trends.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is trading near its 52‑week low, down 9% from the high but up 60.6% from the low, with modest weekly gains after a flat month. The stock’s recent 2.4% dip reflects concerns over growth sustainability. Key focus will be the next quarterly results and progress on AI‑driven product rollouts.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan is modestly up 6.4% YTD and sits 6.5% below its 52‑week peak, comfortably above its low. Daily and weekly gains suggest resilience amid a mixed banking backdrop. Watch net interest margin trends and the bank’s loan‑loss provisions in the upcoming earnings release.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America remains 20.6% under its 52‑week high and 10.8% above its low, with a 7% monthly decline and a 7% YTD drop. The recent dip hints at pressure on net interest income. Investors should monitor Fed rate outlook and the bank’s credit‑quality metrics ahead of earnings.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is trading at its 52‑week high, up 16.9% YTD and 36.8% above its low, buoyed by solid weekly and monthly gains. The stock’s price stability reflects strong payment‑volume growth. The next catalyst is the company’s quarterly volume and fee‑revenue guidance.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard also sits at its 52‑week high, up 10.3% YTD and 31.4% above its low, with consistent weekly and monthly momentum. Payment‑network expansion remains a tailwind. Watch the upcoming earnings for insights on transaction‑volume growth and pricing power.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix is 43.2% below its 52‑week high but 5.2% above its low, having fallen 22.5% YTD with a recent 2.9% daily drop. Subscriber growth and content spend remain focal points. The next earnings report and any updates on price‑tier strategy will be critical.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly trades just 1.8% shy of its 52‑week high, up 58.2% from its low and gaining 16.9% YTD, supported by strong weekly and monthly performance. Momentum is driven by robust drug pipeline sales. Investors should keep an eye on FDA decisions and upcoming sales guidance for new launches.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth is 7.4% below its 52‑week high, up 56.8% from its low and gaining 21.7% YTD, with solid weekly and monthly advances. The health insurer benefits from enrollment growth and cost‑control initiatives. Key watch items include Medicare Advantage enrollment trends and the next earnings outlook on margin pressure.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has rallied 0.9% today but remains 8.2% below its 52‑week high, still 40.5% above its low, reflecting a solid YTD gain of 25.2%. The recent bounce follows a broader 5.4% monthly decline, suggesting the stock is testing support near the low‑end of its range. Investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for clues on whether the recovery can sustain momentum.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart rose 0.8% on the day, trading 11.3% off its 52‑week peak while still 19.1% above its low, and has posted a modest 6% YTD gain. The stock’s strong 11.3% monthly advance signals renewed consumer‑spending confidence. Key focus will be the next same‑store sales report and any updates on its low‑price strategy.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco gained 1.1% and sits 9.5% below its 52‑week high, still 16.9% above its low, delivering a 16.3% YTD return. The 10.6% monthly rise underscores continued demand for bulk retail. Investors should monitor membership renewal trends and any pricing adjustments as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot edged up 0.5% but remains 19.1% under its 52‑week high, though 10.1% above its low, and is down 8.5% YTD. The modest 2.4% monthly gain hints at a possible bottom forming after a broader market pullback. The upcoming housing‑starts data and DIY spending outlook will be pivotal.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil climbed 2.5% to sit exactly at its 52‑week high, still 64.1% above its low, and has surged 48.9% YTD. The 9.6% monthly rise reflects higher oil prices and strong earnings momentum. Watch for crude‑price volatility and the company’s capital‑allocation plan as the next driver.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola rose 2.1% and is trading at its 52‑week high, 41.8% above its low, with a 38.5% YTD gain. The 6.6% monthly increase shows resilience in beverage demand despite broader market softness. Investors should focus on the upcoming earnings beat and any shifts in pricing or product mix.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney slipped 0.1% and is 3.8% below its 52‑week high, still 20.6% above its low, with a flat YTD performance. The 5.0% monthly gain follows a rebound in streaming and park traffic after recent disruptions. The next earnings release and progress on the Disney+ subscriber outlook will be the key watch points.
